M-read-receiver-test expects received Hint/HintHigh to become the readiness SystemCtx. Together these ground preservation of the original admitted context when routing a released status to its origin. They do not require immediate success for every admitted read or preservation of its old index. The suspect sender implementation is the subject of comparison, not the source of the expected output.

feedback.answered: A1: leaders assign term/index to proposals, replicate entries, aggregate remotes and witnesses match positions, and delegate current-term commitment to entryLog.tryCommit. Followers check predecessor term before append and bound propagated commit by the received suffix. A2: campaigning increments term and self-votes; vote grants require log freshness and vote eligibility; candidate replies are deduplicated and observers excluded. Incoming message terms gate dispatch, with higher-term transitions and a check-quorum vote-suppression exception. Reset clears votes, pending read requests and peer progress while retaining log history. Membership application changes the quorum population; removal of the local leader steps it down, and campaigning is blocked while committed work remains unapplied. Engine processing separates free-order sends from post-SaveRaftState sends; application scheduling depends on FastApply, and Peer.Commit acknowledges processed updates. Snapshot restore rejects stale snapshots and either advances a matching prefix or installs a new history; membership restoration is a separate input. Read confirmation has a concrete unresolved correlation discrepancy: readIndex.confirm returns every queued status through the acknowledged context, preserving each status ctx, but handleReadIndexLeaderConfirmation uses the incoming message Hint/HintHigh for every forwarded response whereas local readiness uses each status ctx. This is an implementation observation, not yet an established violation. The apparent observer-confirmation concern is constrained by broadcastHeartbeatMessageWithHint sending nonzero contexts only to voting members; raw handler acceptance alone would omit this producer protection.
remaining: Complete the initial core overview/map with actual log commit enforcement, membership application callers, snapshot completion, and application/client completion paths; present readiness as partial until these connections are read.

For forwarded read responses, determine whether distinct source nodes can have concurrent pending contexts and whether the receiver or client layer remaps/coalesces the returned context. Inspect context generation, response consumption, timeout/retry ownership, and existing tests before fixing a requirement.

Trace delayed replies across membership changes only if producer eligibility and the legal transition history leave a concrete unresolved premise; do not inject an observer confirmation without such history.

feedback.answered: The receiving follower preserves the supplied context, and pendingReadIndex.addReady only updates an exact matching batch. Separate step drains can create concurrent pending contexts; there is no one-outstanding-read guard in the traced admission path. Read confirmation coalescing raises earlier indices but does not change their stored ctx/from. The map now connects both core lines to persistence, accepted membership application, snapshot recovery and client consumption.

formation.explanation: Peer routes proposals to leader. Leader assigns term/index, appends, and sends predecessor-qualified replication; followers match predecessor and protect committed history. Acknowledgements update per-peer matches; majority of full voters and witnesses selects an index whose term must equal current leader term. Commit is propagated via replication and bounded heartbeat commit. Engine persists state and entries before acknowledgement messages, and queues committed entries according to FastApply durability overlap. RSM applies entries and membership, then node callbacks report proposal/read completion. Rejection responses retry earlier suffix; compaction selects snapshot for active peers.

context.explanation: Election timers initiate campaign only for eligible full voters without committed-but-unapplied work. New term resets transient votes/progress/read confirmations; vote granting checks log freshness and prior vote, and candidate forms authority from deduplicated quorum replies. Higher-term protocol messages normally cause stepdown, with check-quorum vote suppression exception; lower terms are ignored. Same-term leader messages demote candidates. Quorum checks, removal and transfer govern loss/change of leadership. Transfer waits for target catchup and triggers target election via TimeoutNow, while blocking proposals until completion or timeout.

connection.explanation: Terms qualify newly counted support, but established committed history survives authority reset and constrains future logs and votes. Membership becomes active through RSM application; campaign defers when applied state lags commit, so a new leader does not simply form using its old unapplied membership. New leader reconstructs pending config status and commits a current-term no-op before multi-voter ReadIndex admission. Pending read contexts are reset with authority; within one leader context, voter heartbeat confirmation releases queue prefixes for local readiness or forwarded replies, and clients require exact context plus applied index. Old network responses are term-filtered and unknown responders rejected; pending client work may independently drop or timeout.

formation.explanation: Peer routes proposals to leader. Leader assigns term/index, appends, and sends predecessor-qualified replication; followers match predecessor and protect committed history. Acknowledgements update per-peer matches; majority of full voters and witnesses selects an index whose term must equal current leader term. Commit is propagated via replication and bounded heartbeat commit. Engine persists state and entries before acknowledgement messages, and queues committed entries according to FastApply durability overlap. RSM applies entries and membership, then node callbacks report proposal/read completion. Rejection responses retry earlier suffix; compaction selects snapshot for active peers.

context.explanation: Election timers initiate campaign only for eligible full voters without committed-but-unapplied work. New term resets transient votes/progress/read confirmations; vote granting checks log freshness and prior vote, and candidate forms authority from deduplicated quorum replies. Higher-term protocol messages normally cause stepdown, with check-quorum vote suppression exception; lower terms are ignored. Same-term leader messages demote candidates. Quorum checks, removal and transfer govern loss/change of leadership. Transfer waits for target catchup and triggers target election via TimeoutNow, while blocking proposals until completion or timeout.

connection.explanation: Terms qualify newly counted support, but established committed history survives authority reset and constrains future logs and votes. Membership becomes active through RSM application; campaign defers when applied state lags commit, so a new leader does not simply form using its old unapplied membership. New leader reconstructs pending config status and commits a current-term no-op before multi-voter ReadIndex admission. Pending read contexts are reset with authority; within one leader context, voter heartbeat confirmation releases queue prefixes for local readiness or forwarded replies, and clients require exact context plus applied index. Old network responses are term-filtered and unknown responders rejected; pending client work may independently drop or timeout.

feedback.answered: The synchronous and asynchronous proposal contracts explicitly distinguish timed-out retries from successful completion: on success the client must call ProposalCompleted before future proposals. Therefore obtaining a successful result, mutating its Data and then reissuing the same completed series is not an applicable retry witness. Existing shallow Result.Data propagation remains an observation, but output mutation/retention rights are still unspecified in the inspected Result and GetResult comments; no cache-integrity obligation is inferred from silence. In contrast, the input-byte-slice reuse contract is explicit, and proposalShard.propose passes nonempty commands through preparePayload with nil destination: uncompressed encoding allocates and copies; Snappy encoding creates a copied result. That actual producer establishes independence from later caller input reuse. A separate session-history reading found a sourced preservation expectation: TestOrderedDoIsLRUOrdered and TestLRUSessionCanBeSavedAndRestoredWithLRUOrderPreserved require eviction order preservation. lrusession.save gathers an ordered ID list and serializes in that order; load re-adds in serialized order. items.rationale:
Reviewed artifact c9313106842f45babd450ec50a1ad648 version 2, including its fixed root launcher and embedded internal/raft helper, against C-forwarded-context version 1 and BD-forwarded-context version 1. The package repair changed only how the same driver is compiled/invoked; the root launcher forwards stdout/stderr and propagates failure. Execution c062d2922ab74798a0e7788936085d88 completed with exit 0 and no changed target files. The raw log, not Go test success, supplies the measured comparison. Both fresh-network scenarios established term 2, commit/applied index 4 and three voters after actual bootstrap, Tick election, voting, replication and no-op commitment. The adapter saves entries/state before delivering messages, commits updates, consumes only initialized membership and no-op entries sequentially, and notifies actual consumed applied progress. Applying bootstrap members again is idempotent in the already bootstrapped Peer; no protocol state, handler or generated message is modified. In-memory TestLogDB substitutes crash-free storage, and no crash or real disk persistence is claimed. One follower request per origin per scenario is issued through Peer.ReadIndex; actual follower forwarding creates the leader queue entries and actual heartbeat producers/responses form confirmation. Later probes are delivered before held earlier probes, and every generated message is eventually drained. M-transport-order explicitly permits out-of-order message batch delivery, so this is within the implementation transport contract rather than an assumed relaxation. The schedule preserves the investigated overlap; it does not serialize it away.

The requirement is supported independently of the suspect sender: M-read-prefix-test checks original ctx/from on each prefix-released status even when index rises, M-read-receiver-test checks transfer of received context to readiness, and the client admission/consumer binds the operation to an exact SystemCtx. The claim concerns a completed response route retaining that key, not unconditional admission-to-success progress. The monitor chooses read_admitted explicitly and correlates by scenario plus origin, which is unique because each of nodes 2 and 3 has only one read in each fresh network. Expected ctx is the original input recorded after real leader admission; observed ctx is copied from the receiving Peer Update ReadyToReads before Commit clears it. No result is suppressed by matching ctx or index. A read-only queue lookup establishes admission, not the outcome.

The retained events show serial node 2 admitted/exported 101:1001 and serial node 3 admitted/exported 202:2002. In overlap, node 2 admission at index 4 was 101:1001, then node 3 admission was 202:2002 with pending_count 2. The leader emitted ReadIndexResp to each destination with 202:2002. Node 2 then exported ReadyToRead 202:2002 at index 4, while node 3 exported its correct 202:2002. Final diagnostics show pending_count 0 and two results in each scenario after all held messages were delivered. Thus the valid violating witness is overlap/origin 2 (monitor event index 13 correlated to admission index 9); the other three comparisons match. There are no parsing errors, missing result fields or ambiguous associations. Source inspection identifies the same cause: confirm retains each s.ctx, but remote routing uses incoming m.Hint/m.HintHigh for every s, while the local branch uses s.ctx. No separate application Lookup or client timeout is observed. The exact mismatch establishes the scoped requirement violation; wider liveness/safety consequences remain excluded rather than inferred from finite draining.

Explained alternatives retained: The serial control preserves both contexts; local leader readiness uses each status context. Queue coalescing may legitimately advance earlier read indices; this checker compares only the context, not an overstrong index equality. Dropped/timed-out client operations are permitted by the API and do not themselves violate this claim. Here the decisive observation is an actually completed exported route with the wrong key.
